# @rxova/ts-extended-errors

> Typed, serializable errors for TypeScript. `ExtendedError` is a base class
> that sets `name`, `code`, `context` and `stack` correctly in subclasses;
> `defineError` creates such a class in one line; five functions search the
> `cause` chain; `serializeError` and `deserializeError` round-trip errors
> through JSON and rebuild them as the original classes. Every function accepts
> `unknown`. Node >= 20.19, no runtime dependencies and no Node.js APIs, so it
> also runs in browsers. MIT. Ships ESM and CommonJS with type declarations.

## Install

Published to GitHub Packages, not npmjs.com. The `.npmrc` of the project that
installs it routes the `@rxova` scope there, with a GitHub token that has
`read:packages`:

    @rxova:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com
    //npm.pkg.github.com/:_authToken=${GITHUB_TOKEN}

Then:

    npm install @rxova/ts-extended-errors

No peer dependencies.

## Minimal working example

```ts
import { defineError, findCauseOf, serializeError, toError } from '@rxova/ts-extended-errors'

const HttpError = defineError('HttpError', { code: 'HTTP' })
const NotFoundError = defineError('NotFoundError', { base: HttpError, code: 'HTTP_NOT_FOUND' })

function loadUser(userId: number) {
  throw new NotFoundError('no such user', { context: { userId } })
}

function loadProfile(userId: number) {
  try {
    return loadUser(userId)
  } catch (cause) {
    throw new HttpError('loading the profile failed', { cause })
  }
}

try {
  loadProfile(42)
} catch (thrown) {
  const error = toError(thrown) // `thrown` is `unknown`, `error` is an `Error`

  const notFound = findCauseOf(error, NotFoundError) // searches the whole chain
  notFound?.code // 'HTTP_NOT_FOUND'
  notFound?.context // { userId: 42 }

  console.log(JSON.stringify(serializeError(error, { includeStack: false })))
  // {"name":"HttpError","message":"loading the profile failed","code":"HTTP","cause":
  //   {"name":"NotFoundError","message":"no such user","code":"HTTP_NOT_FOUND","context":{"userId":42}}}
}
```

## Mistakes to avoid

**1. Passing `context` as the second argument.** The second argument is an
options object. `context` and `cause` are fields of it.

```ts
import { defineError } from '@rxova/ts-extended-errors'

const NotFoundError = defineError<{ userId: number }>('NotFoundError', { code: 'HTTP_NOT_FOUND' })

// WRONG: a type error, `userId` is not an option
// @ts-expect-error
new NotFoundError('no such user', { userId: 42 })

// RIGHT
new NotFoundError('no such user', { context: { userId: 42 } })
```

**2. Calling `defineError` inside a function.** Each call returns a new class,
so `instanceof` against the class from another call is `false`. Define each
error class once, at module scope, and export it.

**3. Calling `deserializeError` without `classes`.** The class is chosen by the
payload's `name`, from the built-in error classes and the ones passed in
`classes`. A name it does not know becomes an `ExtendedError` with that name,
so `instanceof NotFoundError` is `false`.

```ts
import { defineError, deserializeError } from '@rxova/ts-extended-errors'

const NotFoundError = defineError('NotFoundError', { code: 'HTTP_NOT_FOUND' })
const payload = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(new NotFoundError('no such user'))) as unknown

deserializeError(payload) instanceof NotFoundError // false: an ExtendedError named 'NotFoundError'
deserializeError(payload, { classes: [NotFoundError] }) instanceof NotFoundError // true
```

**4. Reading `.code` from a caught value.** In `catch (thrown)`, `thrown` is
`unknown` and may not be an error at all. Use `toError(thrown)` for an `Error`,
`isExtendedError(thrown)` for a type guard, or `findCauseOf(thrown, Class)`,
which also finds an error wrapped in another error's `cause`.

**5. Installing without the scope line in `.npmrc`.** npm then looks for
`@rxova/ts-extended-errors` on npmjs.com and fails with a 404. See Install.

**6. Writing the same message at every throw site.** Give the class a
`message` option instead. The class then takes only the options, and the type
of `context` comes from the parameter of `message`.

```ts
import { defineError } from '@rxova/ts-extended-errors'

// WRONG: every caller repeats the sentence
const LooseDateError = defineError<{ value: string }>('LooseDateError')
new LooseDateError('"2026-02-30" is not a valid date', { context: { value: '2026-02-30' } })

// RIGHT
const InvalidDateError = defineError('InvalidDateError', {
  message: (context: { value: string }) => `"${context.value}" is not a valid date`,
})
new InvalidDateError({ context: { value: '2026-02-30' } })
```

## API

| Export | Kind | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ExtendedError` | class | Base class: `name`, `code`, `context`, `cause`, `stack`, `toJSON()` |
| `isExtendedError` | function | `value instanceof ExtendedError`, as a type guard |
| `defineError` | function | `defineError(name, { code?, base?, message? })` returns a new error class |
| `causeChain` | function | `[error, error.cause, …]`, outermost first |
| `rootCause` | function | The last value in the chain |
| `findCause` | function | The first value in the chain that a predicate accepts |
| `findCauseOf` | function | The first instance of a class in the chain, typed as that class |
| `hasCauseOf` | function | Whether the chain contains an instance of a class |
| `serializeError` | function | A JSON-safe object: `name`, `message`, `code`, `stack`, `context`, `cause`, and an `AggregateError`'s `errors` |
| `deserializeError` | function | Rebuilds `serializeError` output as instances of the original classes |
| `toError` | function | An `Error` for any value; errors are returned unchanged |
| `isErrorLike` | function | Whether a value is an object with a string `message` |
| `describeValue` | function | A one-line string for any value |
| `ErrorContext` | type | `Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>`, the constraint on `context` |
| `ExtendedErrorOptions` | type | `{ cause?: unknown; context?: Context }` |
| `SerializedError` | type | The object `serializeError` returns |
| `SerializedErrorWithProperties` | type | `SerializedError` plus other fields, from `includeOwnProperties: true` |
| `SerializeErrorOptions` | type | `{ maxDepth?, includeStack?, includeOwnProperties?, maxAggregatedErrors? }` |
| `DeserializeErrorOptions` | type | `{ classes?, maxDepth? }` |
| `DefineErrorOptions` | type | `{ code?, base? }` |
| `ExtendedErrorConstructor` | type | The class `defineError` returns |
| `MessageErrorConstructor` | type | The class `defineError` returns with `message`: `new Class({ context, cause })`. Its instances type `context` as present when the throw site must pass one |
| `ExtendedErrorMembers` | type | `name`, `code`, `context` and `toJSON`, added to any `defineError` class |
| `ErrorClass` | type | An error class whose constructor takes `(message, options)` |

## Gotchas

- **`serializeError` includes `stack` by default.** Pass `includeStack: false`
  when the result goes to a client.
- **`includeOwnProperties: true` copies every other own field** of each error in
  the chain, which may include request data.
- **A class with a built-in `base` is not an `ExtendedError`.**
  `defineError(name, { base: RangeError })` has the same members, but
  `instanceof ExtendedError` and `isExtendedError` return `false`.
- **Depth is limited.** `serializeError` and `deserializeError` process 8
  `cause` levels by default; set `maxDepth` to change it.
- **Width is limited too.** `serializeError` keeps 10 of the `errors` of
  `AggregateError`s across the whole output and counts the rest in
  `errorsOmitted`; set `maxAggregatedErrors` to change it.
- **`context` is copied through JSON.** A `Date` in it is serialized as a
  string and a `BigInt` as `'10n'`, and changing the result does not change the
  error.
- **A `message` that throws does not replace the error.** The error is still
  created, with the class name as its message and `context` kept.
- **`deserializeError` keeps the sent message.** A class defined with `message`
  is rebuilt with the payload's `message`; its `message` option is not called.
- **A `message` class always has a `context` object.** The `(message, options)`
  constructor `deserializeError` rebuilds through defaults it to `{}`, so a
  payload that carried none produces `context: {}` rather than `undefined`.
- **`deserializeError` trusts the payload's `name`.** List in `classes` only the
  classes the payload is expected to contain.
